Tenderers must complete the online Single Procurement Document (Scotland) and submit all documents identified in the Invitation to Tender through Public Contracts Scotland by the stated deadline.
The tender return will include:
Appendix 1: Award Questionnaire;
Appendix 2: Pricing Schedule;
Appendix 3: Certificates and Declarations;
Appendix 5: Business Continuity Questionnaire;
applicable Supplier Incentive Service documentation; and
any other information or evidence expressly requested in the Tender Documents or through a formal clarification.
The maximum estimated Contract value of 6.1m GBP excluding VAT is a fixed funding envelope over the full potential five-year term. It includes the ring-fenced Convention Bureau Subvention Fund and does not represent guaranteed expenditure.
Tenderers must propose and justify the amount of the annual budget to be allocated to the Subvention Fund. The Council will retain final approval of the allocation.
Any CPI price adjustment approved under the Contract must be managed within the approved annual funding allocation and maximum Contract value. It will not increase the funding available to the Contract.
All clarification questions must be submitted through the Public Contracts Scotland Question and Answer facility by 12 noon on Friday 18 December 2026.
The Council reserves the right not to accept the lowest-priced or any Tender and may amend, suspend or discontinue the procurement in accordance with the Tender Documents and applicable law.
The Contract will be governed by Scots law and subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Scottish courts.
NOTE: To register your interest in this notice and obtain any additional information please visit the Public Contracts Scotland Web Site at https://www.publiccontractsscotland.gov.uk/Search/Search_Switch.aspx?ID=849075.

Suppliers are advised to allow adequate time for uploading documents and to dispatch the electronic response well in advance of the closing time to avoid any last minute problems.
A sub-contract clause has been included in this contract. For more information see: http://www.publiccontractsscotland.gov.uk/info/InfoCentre.aspx?ID=2363
Community benefits are included in this requirement. For more information see: https://www.gov.scot/policies/public-sector-procurement/community-benefits-in-procurement/

Tenderers will be required to propose proportionate and measurable community benefits linked to the contract. These may include work experience, internships, mentoring and skills development for young people and others seeking careers in tourism, hospitality, events, marketing and the creative industries; engagement with schools, colleges and universities; and opportunities for Aberdeen-based SMEs, third-sector organisations and social enterprises to participate in the supply chain. Commitments accepted through the tender process will be incorporated into the contract and monitored through contract-management arrangements.

tender.title: Aberdeen Destination Marketing, Development and Convention Bureau Service
tender.description:
Aberdeen City Council is seeking to appoint a single contractor to provide an integrated, city-focused Destination Marketing, Development and Convention Bureau Service for Aberdeen.
The Service will support the objectives of the Aberdeen Visitor Levy and the sustainable growth of Aberdeen’s visitor economy. It will include destination marketing and communications, destination development, travel-trade activity, visitor information and welcome services, visitor-economy business engagement, Convention Bureau services, administration of a ring-fenced Convention Bureau Subvention Fund, research, evaluation, data and performance reporting.
The Contract will be for an initial period of three years, with an option for the Council to extend it by up to a further two years. The anticipated commencement date is 1 April 2027.

renewal.description:
The Council may extend the Contract by one or more periods up to a maximum aggregate extension of 24 months.
Any extension will be subject to satisfactory performance, continued requirement, affordability, approved funding and the Council’s applicable governance and decision-making arrangements.

tender.title: Independent Children's Advocacy Service
tender.description:
Dumfries and Galloway Council (the Purchaser) wishes to commission children's advocacy services that:
- are independent and professional;
- provide individual (one-to-one) advocacy that is issue focused; and
- meet statutory requirements and Scottish Executive priorities.
The service will covers such services under the following categories:
- Advocacy services for children and young people who are or have been looked after and accommodated within or outwith the region (excluding those who are placed locally by another Local Authority) up until the age of 26.
- Advocacy for children and young people on the Child Protection Register.
- Advocacy for children and young people in terms of the Mental Health (Care and Treatment) (Scotland) Act 2003.

lots.description:
This procurement is to obtain a suitable advocacy service provider for children's advocacy services. The service objectives are as follows:
To provide an independent and confidential advocacy service to include information, support and advice for Dumfries and Galloway children and young people who are or have been looked after and accommodated within or outwith the region.
To provide access to an advocacy service for children & young people regardless of age, gender, disability, sexual orientation, ethnic origin, faith/religion, or social background.
To match service users and advocates appropriate to each situation’s needs, seeking specialist support where indicated and ensuring service users comfort at all times.
To ensure that children & young people’s own views are heard and adequately represented.
To provide advocacy, related support and information in an age-appropriate and child/young person-centred manner.
To help children and young people to access and understand information relevant to them and make appropriate choices or decisions which give them fuller control of their lives.
To promote choices to young people.
To support children & young people who, because of incapacity or communication difficulties, may not be able to express their needs or views.
To provide advocacy for children and young people who have a mental disorder in compliance with the Mental Health Act.
To guide children and young people towards self-advocacy and avoid creation of dependency.
To develop links with service providers, professionals and relevant support organisations to ensure clear understanding of the role of advocacy.
To develop and promote children and young people’s involvement in service planning.

tender.title: National Framework Agreement for the provision of Sexual Health Services
tender.description:
The demand for accessible, high-quality and innovative sexual health services continues to evolve in response to changing population needs, advances in clinical practice, increasing digital delivery models and the ongoing focus on reducing health inequalities.
The Framework will provide Relevant Authorities with a fully compliant route for the provision of sexual health services, supporting the commissioning of integrated, digital, clinical, diagnostic, prevention, outreach and specialist support services. The Framework is designed to enable Contracting Authorities to secure services that improve public health outcomes, promote early intervention and prevention, support vulnerable populations, and ensure equitable access to care. 
The overall aim of the Framework is to provide a compliant route to market facilitating the procurement of various Sexual Health Services. 
The Framework has been established under The Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023 and The Health Services (Provider Selection Regime) (Wales) Regulations 2025 (and as amended) (together the PSR) for use by all Relevant Authorities (and any future successors to these organisations).
"Relevant Authority" is defined in section 12ZB(7) of the National Health Service Act 2006 and in section 10A(9) of the National Health Service (Wales) Act 2006. It means a combined authority, an integrated care board, a local authority in England, NHS England, an NHS foundation trust or an NHS trust established under section 25 of the National Health Service Act 2006, a county council or county borough council in Wales, a local health board established under section 11 of the National Health Service (Wales) Act 2006, a National Health Service trust established under section 18 of the National Health Service (Wales) Act 2006, or a special health authority established under section 22 of the National Health Service (Wales) Act 2006. 
For the avoidance of doubt, any successor bodies of any of the above entities shall be entitled to place Orders and shall be deemed Relevant Authorities for the purposes of this Framework.
The Framework will be re-opened to new applicants every two years, approximately 90 days before the anniversary of the Framework Commencement Date.

options.description:
HIE reserves the right, on giving reasonable written notice,to require changes to the Services including the removal of Services, the addition of related Services, and increase or decrease in the level of Services, changes to the order in which the Services are to be performed or the locations at which the Services are to be provided. Any modification will be made only where permitted by Regulation 72 of the Public Contracts (Scotland) Regulations 2015.
The circumstances in which the Contract may be modified include:
- changes in building occupany, use or activites that result in an increase or decrease in the reception and support resource required;
- Changes in building opening hours or reception cover requirements that result in an increase or decreae in the days and/or hours during which the Services are required;
- The permanent or temporary relocation of all or part of the Services to another HIE office or premises in Inverness;
-Changes in HIE's available budget that require a reduction in, or enable an increase in, the days or hours of service of the level of reception and associated support resource required, provided these changes remain consistent with the overall nature of the Services;
- Temporary changes to the Services arising from business continuity arrangements, refurbishment, building works, temporary closure or restrictions on access to the premises; and
- Changes to reception duties or associated support activities, provided these reamin consistent with the overall nature of the Services.
-HIE brings the services in-house (fully or partially) such that the services are no longer required  or reduced services are required.
-Reduction or removal of services are required, for example where services are no longer required due to  changes in organisational strategy or priorities
-Cancellation or pausing of a call-off contract due to changes in  project status.
-The addition of similar services, for example due to increased demand, where significant inconvenience and/or substantial duplication of costs to HIE can be avoided.
-Increases to the volume of the services required.
-Change in legislative requirements resulting in increased, reduced or amended services.
-Where demand  under one Lot is lower than anticipated and requirements are instead commissioned under the other Lot, subject always to the overall maximum Framework value not being exceeded.
